chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kazzaz, and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked: A woman left behind her mother, her full sisters (from father and mother), her half-brothers (from mother), and her half-sisters (from father). He said: 'For her full sisters, two-thirds; for her mother, one-sixth; and for her half-sisters from her mother, one-sixth.'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided among full sisters, maternal half-sisters, and the mother?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific shares of female siblings in the presence of a mother, illustrating the Shia jurisprudential application of the Quranic inheritance verses. It highlights the coexistence of the 'full sisters' (who receive two-thirds as residual heirs alongside the father) and 'maternal half-sisters' (who receive one-sixth), demonstrating the precise calculation of fractional shares (*fara'id*) in complex family structures.
